title: Platform guardrails for LLM operators — one-pager
body:
Objective: give a crisp, operator-focused positioning brief that product marketing and solutions teams can use when talking to platform teams and SREs. This is an internal one-pager — not customer-facing copy — designed to align messaging around the unique value Redwood provides to LLM operators who must balance latency, cost, reliability, and regulatory constraints.

Audience: Platform engineers, SREs, infra procurement, and technical buyer personas at mid-market & enterprise where inference economics and uptime matter. Also useful for field and solutions folks preparing technical discovery.

Core claim (single sentence): Redwood is the inference platform that makes running production LLMs predictable and safe by applying engineering-grade guardrails that reduce cost volatility, protect SLAs, and simplify operational decisions across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Why this matters to operators (problem framing):
- Explosion of model choices and rapid model churn makes head-to-head evaluation expensive and error-prone for infra teams.
- Naive self-hosting or unmanaged endpoints create unpredictable token costs and capacity spikes that break external SLAs.
- Security/compliance requirements + multi-region performance demands force teams to juggle different stacks for dev, staging, and prod.
- Operators need deterministic levers (not just opaque "optimization suggestions") to trade latency vs cost under SLO constraints.

Redwood’s operator-first differentiators (positioning bullets):
1) Deterministic runtime controls: explicit batching, cache policies, and quantization profiles operators can pin to routes and roll out gradually. These are presented as actionable knobs (not hidden heuristics).
2) Unified policy plane: single place to declare routing rules (latency vs cost vs region vs tier), with safe fallbacks and automated canaries so infra teams can test changes without firing alarms.
3) Cost predictability features: token-level cost breakdowns, preflight capacity estimators, and autoscale policies that guarantee throughput windows for reserved pools.
4) Private-friendly operations: VPC control plane option, KMS/HSM integrations, and air-gapped packaging for regulated customers minimizing lift for compliance.
5) Observability that maps to operational workflows: per-route latency histograms, traceable KV cache hit rates, and regression alerts tied to prompt-eval suites so SREs can correlate quality changes to infra changes.

Proof points (concise evidence):
- Benchmarks: consistent p50/p95 latency within target windows across three model classes (chat, generation, rerank) in multi-region tests (internal benchmark deck ref).
- Cost: customers reduced per-token cost variance by >40% after enabling autoscale + caching on bursty workloads (field case: fintech beta customer, anonymized).
- Reliability: built-in fallback policies prevented production outages during a regional GPU shortage on a pilot rollout (postmortem summarized in ops playbook).
- Compliance: successful Private deployment with FIPS-compatible KMS integration for a regulated healthcare pilot (legal review completed).

How to frame the tradeoff conversation with buyers (talking tracks):
- If they lead with latency: emphasize kernel selection, runtime optimizations, and canary routing that preserves p95 targets while introducing model upgrades.
- If they lead with cost: emphasize batching, prefix caching, and the Optimize toolkit that yields measurable unit economics improvements with clear rollback paths.
- If they lead with compliance: highlight Private deployment options, audit logging, and straightforward KMS/HSM plugs.

Objection handling (short templates):
- "We can self-host for cheaper": call out unknowns — maintenance cost, subtle correctness regressions when updating kernels, and lack of a unified policy plane that leads to configuration drift. Offer a migration checklist and TCO comparator.
- "We already have a managed endpoint": ask about SLOs during peak, rollback behavior, and per-token cost visibility. Redwood’s explicit guardrails and fallback policies reduce operational blast radius.
- "We need air-gapped/on-prem": note Redwood Private is designed for this use case; suggest a technical discovery to map network and audit requirements.

Customer story snippets (for field use):
- "A payments platform reduced inference cost jitter by 35% and eliminated tail-latency spikes after switching inference routing to Redwood’s dedicated pools and enabling prefix cache."
- "A healthcare customer completed a Private pilot with FIPS KMS and maintained identical dev-to-prod APIs while meeting their audit checklist."

Key metrics to track for GTM (recommended):
- Time to deterministic SLO attainment (days to reach target p95 under production traffic)
- Percent reduction in per-token cost variance after enabling caching/autoscale
- Number of successful canary rollouts vs rollback incidents (safety score)
- Private deployment lead-to-pilot conversion rate

Risks and open questions (internal):
- Messaging risk: operator language can sound dry; need a companion one-pager with customer-facing outcomes (reduced MTTR, spend predictability, fewer outages) that sales can use.
- Competitive claims overlap: several competitors push "managed endpoints" messaging — we must keep the conversation practical and technical (show knobs).
- Product gaps: tighten docs and templates for ops playbooks (runbooks for canaries, fallback rules). Action item: product docs ticket (DOCS-217).

Next steps (who does what):
- GTM: create two-slide cheat sheet for SDR/AE focusing on 3 quick discovery questions and 2 proof points (owner: Ravi, due: 2025-02-14).
- Solutions: build a 30-minute technical discovery template and checklist for Private pilots (owner: Elena, due: 2025-02-28).
- Product: prioritize runbook templates and add a "safe change" guide to the console (owner: Tom, linked ticket: DOCS-217).

Notes to self (work-in-progress tone):
- Keep this one-pager short; it should sit in the enablement folder and be the canonical operator framing.
- Need to validate the benchmark numbers above with bench team (ping: bench-team@redwood.ai).
- Consider making a short demo flow that shows changing a routing policy and safely rolling back (high impact for field calls).

-- end of brief --
